title: Thermal FK–Ising interfaces and massive SLE

issues.location: Prop. 2.1 / Prop. 3.1 (inputs from Park); Sec. 2 thermal-angle definition
issues.description: The sign and normalization that link m>0 (via the elliptic-angle prescription and r_δ/δ→|m|/2) to the continuum equation ∂̄f + i m f̄ = 0, and hence to Δh = −4m|∇h| and a nonnegative drift C ≥ 0, are taken entirely from Park. The paper also notes that Park's printed prefactor drops a factor i. I could not check these conventions against the cited source. The proof is internally consistent, but which sign of m gives which drift direction depends on this external convention.
issues.evidence: Footnote in Sec. 3.1: 'The printed prefactor in [Park, Eq. (2.1)] omits this factor; we use its projection and square-integral conventions.' Everything downstream (Q≥0, C≥0, h≥u) depends on the sign of the mass term.

coverage:
Read every section. Checked in detail:
- Model and continuum definition: BVP uniqueness via the drift-comparison diffusion (the β identity); chart-scaling remark C→C/λ.
- Calculus: Hadamard formula ∂_tG=−(2/π)P(z)P(w); cutoff loss dχ(Y/λ); Itô formula d(Φ'/(πZ)) with coefficient (d[W^M]−4dt)/Z³; explicit DG kernel and its limit P(v)/π; derivation of identities (cal:identity-zero/martingale/drift) including the factors 4 and 8 and the −2Cτ/z² kernel-loss term; tip-expansion bounds (subharmonic sup of μ, Cauchy–Schwarz against ρ, Young near-part, far-part dominated convergence); pole comparison (cubic order gives |U|²=16τ/3, quadratic order gives ν=(2π/3)Cτ, singular-clock elimination ν=0 on τ=0). I independently re-derived the drift 2πC/3 heuristically from the F~(πz)^{-1/2}(1+πCz/2) martingale.
- Energy section: clock identities (Y_s=Y_0e^{-2s}, dlog crad=−4X²ds); reflected-ball ODE ∂_t(l''/l')=4l'/(l−W)³ and distortion; supremum tail, tightness, small-power contraction, bin interpolation exponents, shell Cauchy–Schwarz and change of variables μ²dA(v)=m²dA(w).
- Uniqueness: stopped-Girsanov argument with first energy level.
- Localization: gate counting and product asymptotics; negative-mass duality (the sine weights swap exactly).
Only skimmed: the G2/arm-comparison proofs, the fermion sign-lifting argument (Prop. geo:martingale), the covariance-clock Hilbert construction, and the shielding topology. Park's and Kemppainen–Smirnov's results are taken as black boxes.
main_claim: For every bounded simply connected marked domain, every nonzero mass, and every family of uniformly angle-bounded isoradial lattices (marked Carathéodory approximation, diameters possibly unbounded), thermal FK–Ising interfaces converge along the full sequence in the normalized-disc curve metric. For m>0 the limit is the unique finite-energy weak solution of dW=√(16/3)dB+(2π/3)C_t dt, where C_t=(4/π)∫P μ_t|∇(h_t∘ψ_t)| and h_t solves Δh=−4m|∇h|. For m<0 the limit is given by duality and reversal.
sibling_notes: Family 223 siblings (Square-lattice FK, Conformal limits, Quenched FK-Ising, Natural occupation measures) are separate square-lattice/critical papers. This paper does not cite them: its inputs are Park (massive observable plus near-critical RSW) and Kemppainen–Smirnov. So it does not inherit the CONFIRMED CRITICAL hol:strict-budget issue flagged for the Square-lattice FK interfaces paper.
